verdict.reasoning: Patient reports waking with a bad left-sided headache around 5:30: "woke up this morning... really horrible pain on the left side of my head" and "Probably around 5:30ish."
Patient states current headache is more severe than previous: "I've had a bit of a history with headaches but nothing as severe as this before." and it woke him early.

Past headaches described as frontal and not strictly one-sided: "Not so much on the one side. It tends to be a bit of a cluster at the front of my head... normally they kind of spread across the front of my head." This supports prior milder, more bilateral/frontal cluster-type headaches.
Light sensitivity reported: when asked about bright lights, patient says, "I'm a little bit sensitive. It... makes my eyes a little bit sore."
Eye soreness with headache is explicitly mentioned: "I'm a little bit sensitive. It just, it kind of makes my eyes a little bit sore."
Dizziness on waking that resolved: "when I first got up this morning my head felt a bit dizzy, but that's kind of... seems to be fine."
Headache ultimately better when lying down: patient says it is initially sore but then eases, and when asked, replies, "Yeah, I would say so" to it being better lying down.
History of anxiety: "I had, like, anxiety for about two years now and I've been on Sertraline for a while."
Patient confirms taking sertraline: "I've been on Sertraline for a while" and to "Are you taking [sertraline] at the moment?" he answers "Yes."
Current medication status is clear: in response to "Are you taking searching at the moment?" patient says "Yes."
Paracetamol use and lack of effect: "I've taken some paracetamol." and to "Has that helped?" he replies, "Not really, no."
Doctor plans to start ibuprofen: "the things that we start off first line if someone had migraine would be to start ibuprofen."
Doctor allows continued paracetamol: "You can keep on taking paracetamol as well if you like, but the ibuprofen is actually more effective for migraine."
No known drug allergies: "Do you have any allergies to any medication?" Patient: "Not that I'm aware of, no."
Maternal history of anxiety: "My mum's had a history of anxiety as well, but no kind of like physical illnesses..."
Work-related stress and late nights: "Work's kind of a bit stressful... lot of kind of a backlog of work... I've kind of been doing a lot of late nights as well."
Non-smoker: "Are you a smoker?" Patient: "No."
Regular running: "So normally I try to go running at least three times a week."
Lives with partner: "I live with my partner."
Doctor considers tension vs migraine: "it sounds like it might be one of two things. It could be an element of what we call tension headache... The other possibility is migraine as well."
Stress/anxiety linked to tension headache: "what makes that more likely is the fact that you've been under some pressure and you have a history of anxiety in the past." (said about tension headache).

Unilateral pain and light sensitivity linked to migraine: "The other possibility is migraine as well. And the fact what makes that more likely is the fact it's on one side and that you've got some sensitivity to light."
Plan is ibuprofen plus optional paracetamol: "start ibuprofen... You can keep on taking paracetamol as well if you like."
Time off work suggested: "maybe consider taking some time off work... maybe having a week off if you self certify that might help with things."
Counseling and self-referral link: "I'd also like you to explore counseling options as well. So there's counseling service in your area that I can give you the link for you to self refer."
Sleep advice: "ensure that you're having a minimum of 7, 8 hours sleep at night, every night."
Fluid intake advice: "A minimum of 1.5 to 2 liters of water or fluids a day, and that's not including coffee or tea."
Follow-up in a week: "we'll have a follow up in a week's time" and later "we'll touch base in a week's time with me, myself, or one of the other doctors."

Low threshold to seek reassessment: "If anything changes in the meantime or you get worried or things get worse, feel free. Have a low threshold for ringing us back and booking an appointment and we can reassess."
No neck stiffness: "Do you have any neck stiffness at all?" Patient: "No."
No fever: "do you have any fever?" Patient: "No."

No nausea currently; vomiting not mentioned: "Are you feeling nauseous at all?" Patient: "Not really..." No vomiting reported in transcript, so stating no nausea/vomiting is consistent with the available information.
No self-harm thoughts: when asked, "Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself or hurting yourself?" patient answers, "No."
